text:
sylvia: @channel Customer support flagged a spike in API p99 for the EU inference endpoint starting ~09:10 UTC. Multiple users reporting ~700-1200ms TLS handshake delays, overall request p99 up from ~220ms to ~900ms. I have one repro from a customer in APAC hitting eu-west endpoint. Can we triage? :warning:

jonathan: on it. any sample request ids or client IPs?

sylvia: sample request-id: req_2026-03-15_09:12:34_az1. client IP: 203.0.113.54. Support attached a curl timing: `curl -w "time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_total:%{time_total}
" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` returned: `time_connect:0.120 time_appconnect:0.950 time_total:1.050`

maria: that's TLS handshake taking ~830ms (time_appconnect - time_connect). Looks like SYN->TLS/ServerHello delay. Could be cross-region hop or an MTU/path issue.

jonathan: running traceroute from our EU POPs to the client IP, and from APAC POP to EU POPs. Sharing outputs.

jonathan: `traceroute to 203.0.113.54 (203.0.113.54), 30 hops max`:
1  10.12.0.1  0.2 ms  0.2 ms  0.2 ms
2  198.51.100.1  1.1 ms  1.0 ms  1.2 ms
3  * * *
4  203.0.113.1  180.4 ms  179.9 ms  180.1 ms

jonathan: Notice hop 4 is high when tracerouting from apac-pop to eu-west-pop.

alex: I ran mtr from the eu-west edge host towards the client, zero issues: average latency 24ms, no packet loss. But from apac-edge -> eu-west edge path we see occasional high tail latency ~160-300ms and some retransmits.

maria: can you run `openssl s_client -connect api.eu-west.redwood:443 -servername api.redwood.example -msg -debug` from apac edge and eu edge and capture ClientHello/ServerHello timing? We want to know if ServerHello is delayed or TCP handshake is delayed.

jonathan: pasted logs:
-- apac-edge openssl timing snippet --
TCP handshake complete: 0.110s
ClientHello sent: +0.000s
ServerHello received: +0.820s
-- eu-edge openssl timing snippet --
TCP handshake complete: 0.018s
ClientHello sent: +0.000s
ServerHello received: +0.025s

jonathan: That confirms server is fast in eu, but apac-edge path sees a ~700–800ms gap between ClientHello and ServerHello. That usually means the packet got steered to a different egress/ingress pair or hit an intermediate appliance delaying TLS.

sre-bot: detected route-change event at 2026-03-15T09:08:12Z affecting peering peer-ix-5: BGP update flaps -> local preference recompute.

maria: BGP/peering change could cause an anycast mapping shift: client IP might be routed to eu node but TLS response routed back via a different colo, causing cross-zone hairpin. We should check our edge logs for mismatched src/dst AS paths and TLS SNI-landings.

jonathan: pulled ingress logs for the request-id: `ingress-log req_2026-03-15_09:12:34_az1`: shows SYN from 203.0.113.54 hit apac-edge1, but TLS ServerHello came from eu-west-02 (different POP id).

sylvia: so packet reached apac-edge, then upstream routing returned to eu-west server for TLS. That explains extra latency. Any idea why the return path chose eu-west?

jonathan: likely route selection on our transit provider or their upstream. BGP change at 09:08 triggered a temporary less-specific path announcement that made some AS choose eu-west egress. I can confirm by checking our BGP updates and the transit provider's syslog.

alex: mitigation options? Can we force clients bound to apac to prefer apac region temporarily?

maria: short-term mitigations: 1) announce more specific prefixes from APAC POPs (if we can) to steer traffic back, 2) temporarily adjust local-preference with transit to prefer apac egress for affected prefixes, 3) reduce DNS TTL for edge anycast answers so we can shift quickly (but that impacts cache). Also we can enable immediate fallback to secondary regional instance in the control plane for affected customers.

jonathan: I pushed a temporary route preference change with transit partner at 09:26 UTC to prefer APAC egress for the /24s. Monitoring now.

sre-bot: alert: route-preference-change applied (ticket rtpref-987). Peering provider confirmed acceptance at 2026-03-15T09:27:03Z.

support-bot: notified affected customers: ticket #INC-4421.

sylvia: after the route change I re-ran the curl repro from APAC client: `time_connect:0.110 time_appconnect:0.045 time_total:0.160`. Great — appconnect is now lower than connect (server responded locally), total 160ms.

maria: p99 across EU endpoint dropped from ~900ms to ~210ms over the 09:30–09:35 window according to metrics.

alex: monitoring shows no packet loss and stable TLS handshake times now. I'll keep the route preference change for 45m while we watch BGP stability. If it holds, we can update the route announcements and coordinate with transit to prevent recurrence.

jonathan: root cause summary draft: transient BGP route flap at transit peer caused return traffic to be routed to a distant POP (eu-west) while client flowed into local APAC POP, producing cross-POP TLS hairpin and large handshake tail latency. Confirmed by traceroute, openssl timings, ingress logs showing different POPs for SYN and ServerHello, and BGP update event.

sylvia: creating follow-up action items: 1) postmortem (ENG-789) — owner: jonathan, due EOD+2; 2) update playbook with checklist for route-preference mitigation — owner: maria, due EOD+3; 3) ask transit to review BGP dampening/anycast stability — owner: alex, due EOD+5; 4) add automated detection: correlate ClientHello/ServerHello POP mismatch (SRE-runbook) — owner: sylvia, due EOD+7.

sre-bot: created postmortem ENG-789 and linked INC-4421.

support-bot: customer update: "We've routed your traffic back to the nearest POP and are monitoring. Expect latencies to return to normal within minutes. We'll follow up with a write-up." :thumbsup: 

maria: quick note — as long-term fix we should consider: (a) refine anycast health checks to avoid blackholing during BGP churn, (b) shorter BGP MRAI for critical prefixes with select peers, (c) more visibility into cross-POP TLS handshake mapping.

jonathan: I'll collect BGP dump + pcap of the flow for the postmortem.

sylvia: thanks team. Adding reaction :eyes: and closing this slack thread. If anyone has other follow-ups add to ENG-789.

alex: thumbs up.

sre-bot: thread marked resolved at 2026-03-15T10:01:40Z."
